name: fx-63eb255a-blind30
instr:
# fx-regen

This is a terminal browser for structured data documents: you hand it a file, it draws the contents as a foldable tree, and from there you move about with the arrow buttons, jump to a numbered row, type queries, fold and unfold, take entries out, ask for the result in another shape, and let a shell offer you suggestions as you type. Almost every one of those is now wrong somewhere. The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Opening a file and letting the very first screen draw is already enough to see it. A lone document handed over is presented with one extra container around it, as though several documents had been streamed in one after another. The dotted address worked out for the selected entry is built as if it never began at the document root, so the addresses handed around no longer agree with the file, and the same flaw shows again the moment the whole document is folded shut with shift and the left arrow. Ordinary text is altered on its way to the screen as well: the step that rewrites accented letters into their plain lookalikes now reaches letters far outside the band it was meant for. A percentage-style figure drawn alongside the document is worked out against a scale one larger than a hundred, so it reads slightly off at every position. And starting the program and pressing the down arrow three times, with nothing else done at all, yields a screen no button press can explain: a table assembled once while the program boots begins at
